dedupe_keys.name: sustain lc liquid cooling control benchmark frontier

description: Sustain-LC is a benchmarking environment for end-to-end control of the liquid cooling of a large data centre, built on a Modelica model of the cooling system of the Frontier supercomputer at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The Modelica plant is compiled as FMU 2.0 units and co-simulated through PyFMI, and agents control pump speeds, temperature set points, valve positions and cooling-tower settings across blade groups and cabinets while being scored on energy, temperatures and constraint violations. It includes reinforcement learning agents based on PPO with multi-agent and multi-head variants, a conventional controller following ASHRAE Guideline 36, policy distillation into decision trees, and explainable agents built on open large language models. It was released by Hewlett Packard Enterprise as part of the high-performance supercomputing digital twin led by ORNL, and is linked to the LC-Opt paper on benchmarking reinforcement learning and agentic AI for liquid cooling (arXiv 2511.00116, 2025). Coverage: one reference system, Frontier's cooling plant, driven by workload power and weather. Format and access: Python code, FMUs and notebooks on GitHub; free of charge under the MIT licence. Caveats: the plant model is specific to Frontier and HPE Cray cooling; training agents is computationally heavy; results in the paper are simulations, not field trials. Simulation uses: optimisation and digital-twin control of data-centre cooling, and exposure of cooling capacity to hot weather or equipment faults. Related records: ExaDigiT provides the digital twin, SustainDC covers air-cooled facilities, AlphaDataCenterCooling models a chilled-water plant.
